idea.body: Mental arithmetic swaps the written method for a friendly-number trick, done in your head. Round a tricky number to a nearby multiple of ten, do the easy calculation, then adjust the result back by however much you rounded. Doubling, breaking a number into tens and ones, and multiplying by 5, 9 or 25 through a shortcut all follow the same idea. Turn the problem into an easier one, then fix up the small difference at the end. Adding 98 and 47: round 98 up to 100, add to get 147, then take back the 2 you added, landing on 145.

workedExample.prompt: What is 98 plus 47, worked out in your head?
steps: You added 2 more than 98 really has, so take that 2 back.

ways.name: Round then adjust back
ways.when: Use this when one number is just a little away from a friendly multiple of ten.
steps: Round the tricky number up or down to the nearest ten.
Do the easier calculation with that rounded number.
Add back or take away the small amount you rounded by.
ways.trap: Adjusting in the wrong direction, adding the rounding amount instead of taking it back.

ways.name: Bridge through ten
ways.when: Use this when adding two numbers whose ones digits pass ten together.
steps: Split the second number into a piece that completes the first to the next ten, and what is left over.
Add the piece that completes the ten.
Add the leftover piece to that ten.
ways.trap: Splitting the second number by the wrong amount, so the first addition does not land on a whole ten.

figure.alt: A number line from 38 to 64 with a jump of plus 2 to reach 40, then a jump of plus 24 to reach 64.

frames.caption: Split into a piece to reach ten.
Add the piece that completes the ten.
Add the leftover piece to that ten.

ways.name: Near doubles
ways.when: Use this when two numbers being added are close to each other.
steps: Find the double of the smaller number.
Work out how much bigger the other number is.
Add that difference to the double.
ways.trap: Doubling the wrong number, or forgetting to add the small difference back on.

ways.name: Split into tens and ones
ways.when: Use this when multiplying a two-digit number by a single digit in your head.
steps: Split the two-digit number into tens and ones.
Multiply the tens part by the single digit.
Multiply the ones part by the single digit.
ways.trap: Adding the two partial results incorrectly instead of lining up their place values.

bank.prompt: A rover collects rock samples over several days. One count is 47 and another is 29. In your head, what is the total?
explanation: 29 is close to 30, just 1 less.
47 plus 30 is 77.
Take back the extra 1 you added: 77 minus 1 is 76.
bank.useAgain: when one number in an addition is close to a friendly multiple of ten.
hints: Round the trickier number to the nearest ten first, and remember by how much you moved it.
Add the rounded number, then adjust the total back by that same amount, in the opposite direction.
bank.socraticHint: If you round a number up to add it, do you then add or take away the extra at the end?
